subject: Follow-up: Model readiness & prompt pack for eval
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Model readiness & prompt pack for eval

Hi Emily —

Great to meet you and the PaperTrail team earlier. Quick recap + concrete next steps from our side so we can kick off a short eval: 

Summary of call:
- Goal: Replace current keyword heuristics with an LLM assistant for log summarization, triage, and runbook suggestion.
- Success metrics: 85% precision on triage labels; avg. summary length 40–70 tokens; end-to-end latency < 650ms p95 for single-log queries.
- Primary constraints: PII redaction required, on-prem data staging for ground truth, and deterministic regression checks.

Recommended initial models for evaluation:
- redwood-rlm-7b-quant (recommended for cost/latency trade-off)
- open-7b-pt (if you need fully open-weight reproducibility)
- redwood-13b-fp16 (if higher quality needed for summarization benchmarks)

Benchmarks & artifacts I attached/linked:
- Short bench: token latency and throughput expectations (link below)
- Prompt schema template (attached) — please populate with representative customer prompts and edge cases

Asks / next steps for PaperTrail:
1) Share a batch (~500) of representative prompts/queries covering edge cases, low-frequency errors, and intentionally ill-formed logs. Prefer CSV with columns: id, user_query, expected_label, redact_fields. See attached prompt_schema_template.csv
2) Identify any PII categories we must aggressively redact (e.g., API keys, IPs, user emails) and flag examples in the sample set. If you prefer, we can sign an addendum NDA/mutual redaction agreement.
3) Send an S3 link or secure upload for the prompts (we'll provide a pre-signed PUT) and confirm access window.

What Redwood will deliver once we have the prompts:
- Eval pack with 3 model variants + per-model benchmarks vs your metrics (precision/recall, summary length, latency p50/p95)
- Suggested prompt-level redaction and a small guardrail for hallucination-sensitive outputs
- Regression test harness to run on future model/quant changes (we surface any quality drops)

Timeline suggestion: you upload prompts by 2025-12-24 -> Redwood returns initial eval within 4 business days -> 2026-01-03 for follow-up. Let us know if you need an expedited window.

Attachments: prompt_schema_template.csv

Thanks — I cc'd Marissa (model evaluation lead) and Ben (solutions) so they can weigh in on the redaction checklist and sample pack format.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: prompt_schema_template.csv (CSV template: id,user_query,expected_label,redact_fields,notes)

From: Emily Zhang <emily@papertrail.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-18T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model readiness & prompt pack for eval

Thanks, Irene — great summary.

We can assemble the sample set. A couple of notes/questions from our side:
- Security: we need guidance on which fields you consider PII vs. contextual log content (e.g., stack traces often contain file paths and function names which we want kept).
- The procurement/ops team prefers uploads to our secure bucket. I'll loop procurement and share a pre-approved S3 path.
- Timeline: we can get an initial 200-300 prompts by 12/22, but full 500 may slip to 12/28 depending on internal approvals.

Attaching a small example CSV with 12 rows to show current export format.

Emily
Emily Zhang
Head of Product | PaperTrail AI
---
Attachment: customer-sample-prompts.csv (12 rows)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@papertrail.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-18T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model readiness & prompt pack for eval

Hi Emily — looping in a few practical items from the eval side. Short answers up-front, fuller notes below.

Short redaction guidance (recommendation):
- Required redact: API keys, bearer tokens, user identifiers (email, username), full IP addresses (retain /24 mask if needed), and session IDs.
- Optional retain: filenames, function names, error codes (these are useful for signal).
- For any ambiguous fields, include a sample with a mask column in the CSV (see "redact_fields").

Model & eval recommendations:
- Start with redwood-rlm-7b-quant for 1st pass: good token economics and sub-500ms typical single-request latency on our Dedicated stacks.
- If you see consistent failure modes with summarization (truncation or missing context), run redwood-13b-fp16 as a higher-quality check.
- We'll run 3 automatic checks: label precision/recall, summary brevity/consistency, and hallucination rate (heuristic+human spot checks).

Files and links:
- Redaction checklist (attached): redaction-checklist.pdf
- Drive playbook on prompt-level redaction and masking: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3credaction
- HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Actionable next steps for Emily / PaperTrail:
1) Send the prompt CSV to the S3 path you mentioned (we'll accept encrypted bucket uploads). If easier, we can provide a presigned PUT link.
2) Mark edge cases in the CSV with notes column (e.g., "multiline exception, contains email in stacktrace").
3) Confirm whether you want on-prem staging (we have a Private deployment option) or Hosted eval. Hosted is faster to run; Private gives no telemetry to our hosted control plane (useful for regulated logs).

Sampling plan once we receive data:
- We will sample for long-tail failure modes and create a 50-case edge case set for manual review. That will feed prompt re-writes and guardrail rules.

If it's helpful, Ben can set up a 30-min walkthrough of the upload process and the CSV template later this week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Applied ML — Eval Lead | Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redaction-checklist.pdf

From: Emily Zhang <emily@papertrail.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-12-18T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model readiness & prompt pack for eval

Thanks Marissa / Irene — that's helpful and aligns with our compliance needs.

I'll: 
- Upload the 12-row sample (attached) to our secure bucket and share the link by EOD.
- Work with procurement to clear the full 500 prompt export and aim for 12/28 delivery; if procurement slows us, we'll at minimum send a 300-prompt interim set by 12/22.
- Flag any samples that include email addresses or API tokens; we'll replace with <REDACTED> and populate the redact_fields column per your template.

Let's tentatively schedule a 30-min upload walkthrough on 2025-12-19 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for Ben?

Emily
